Video formula audit

Compared against all 10 numbered scenes in your supplied Matharium video, JmivLg-1vTzbhlxE.mp4. Related ingredients were present in the original 160-family collection, but none of these complete constructions was an exact preset.

Eight visible constructions are implemented. Two layered constructions are explicitly marked as reconstructions: the video displays y₂ = 2 + cₛ/12 but never supplies the list c. Their formulas are covered, with an original replacement melody rather than an assertion of exact note-for-note playback.

Replacement c, indexed from zero: (0,3,7,5,3,0,3,5,7,10,8,7,5,3,0,−2,0,3,7,5,3,0,−2,0,3,5,7,5,3,0,−2,0).

For equations using b = ⌊x/4⌋ + 2, lists use one-based b on −4 ≤ x < 12; the app holds the last block at the right endpoint. This keeps every displayed block defined. The video does not label its axis range. Other examples use −8…8. Negative modulo uses a nonnegative remainder.

Formula coverage does not imply identical audio: Sonograph supplies its own synthesis, voices, and scan timing.

The kick roll 1 · 00:02

Visible equation implemented; equality at x mod 4 = 3 assigned to the final branch.

y = −1.6 + 5 e−k(x mod p)

(k,p) = (7,1) when x mod 4 < 2; (14,0.5) when 2 ≤ x mod 4 < 3; (28,0.25) otherwise. The video leaves equality at 3 unspecified; this app uses the final branch.

Earlier coverage: Exponential pulse train. Missing the variable (k,p) schedule.

The cowbell 2 · 00:08

Two-voice reconstruction: the video does not supply the c melody list.

y₁ = −1.6 + mb/12 + 3.6 e−14(x mod 2)
y₂ = 2 + cs/12

m = (0,0,−4,−2); b = ⌊x/4⌋ + 2; s = ⌊4x⌋ mod 32. The video omits c; this app substitutes the original 32-step melody listed in the reference notes. Index s is interpreted from zero. Both curves play together.

Earlier coverage: Decay and stepped contours existed separately. Missing the simultaneous second voice and block offsets.

q = ⌊4x⌋/4; u = 1.8 sin(πq/2) + 1.2 sin(3πq/4) − 0.75.

A whole drum beat 5 · 00:26

All visible branches implemented; undefined intervals are silent.

0.6 + 3 e−25r, r < 0.45 and j = 1

Earlier composition additions

The current listening collection trims some of these earlier additions and adds sixteen new musical constructions. Their saved preset links still work.

These are original combinations, separate from the video reference examples. They add long-short pulses, changing subdivisions, polymeter, logarithmic oscillation, cubic curves, smooth interpolated steps, gated packets, rational phase bends, restarting sweeps, waveform crossfades, mirrored pulse codes, and bounded phase warps.

  • Swing kick pair: Long-short pairs of exponential drops give the curve a swinging pulse.
  • Ratchet bursts: One, two, four, then eight short pulses repeat within successive blocks.
  • Three against five: Pulse trains with three and five hits interfere in a repeating polyrhythm.
  • Log-periodic ripple: Oscillations bunch around a movable center on a logarithmic scale.
  • Bézier ribbon: Repeated cubic Bézier segments rise and dip with asymmetric control heights.
  • Hermite glide steps: Cubic smoothstep joins a repeating four-note contour without pitch jumps.
  • Raised-cosine packets: Separated sine packets open and close with rounded cosine edges.
  • Rational phase bend: A bounded rational phase warp alternately squeezes and relaxes a sine.
  • Resetting glissando: Each repeated cell sweeps faster before starting over.
  • Sine-to-triangle morph: A slow crossfade reshapes rounded lobes into angular triangles.
  • Palindrome pulse code: A mirrored eight-cell rhythm alternates high and low decay shapes.
  • Pendulum phase warp: A bounded arctangent phase modulation creates alternating tight and broad curls.
